name: Fist to Five Consensus
deliverable: Rapid non-binary consensus calibration and identification of dissent

steps.text: Explain the scale: a fist blocks, one or two means reservations, three agrees, and four or five actively supports.
State the proposal in one sentence and give everyone a silent moment to choose a number.
Count down and reveal together, with eyes closed or screens hidden, so no one reads the room first.
Go to the lowest hand, ask what single change would raise it to three, then revise the proposal.
Re-vote once. When no fist or one remains, record the decision as made and stop chasing fives.

failure: The room chases unanimity, spending the session lifting threes to fives while a real blocker in the corner goes unheard.
intervention: Say consensus means no blocking dissent, not equal enthusiasm. Ask the lowest hand what would move it to three, then re-vote.
provenance: Source protocol: the steps follow the written script in the source.

origin.note: Widely used in consent-based decision practice; no single documented originator.
